title: A developer's guide to the OpenAI Agents SDK
summary: Learn how to build with the OpenAI Agents SDK in Python, from tools, handoffs, guardrails, and sessions to tracing, costs, and sandboxed code execution.
body_markdown:
OpenAI's Agents SDK is an open-source runtime for AI agents in Python and TypeScript. Every example targets` openai-agents` 0.24.0, which[PyPI lists as released](https://pypi.org/project/openai-agents) on October 15, 2026 (UTC). The SDK is still pre-1.0, and minor versions can carry breaking changes.


A working agent combines a function tool, a handoff, an input guardrail, a session, and traces. Things change once that agent writes code and runs it.[Agent-generated code](https://blaxel.ai/blog/how-do-ai-agents-execute-code) belongs inside an isolated sandbox.


## Key takeaways


- Each handoff passes the full conversation history by default, so budget runs with several agents separately from single agent tests.
- Minor OpenAI Agents SDK releases can carry breaking changes before 1.0, so pin exact versions and test every upgrade.
- Run code the agent generates in a microVM with its own kernel, away from the process holding your credentials.
- Baseten Sandboxes are a first-class sandbox provider, and` SandboxRunConfig` attaches them at run time so agent definitions stay portable.


## What is the OpenAI Agents SDK?


An AI agent is a model that decides which tools to call, and in what order, to finish a task. The OpenAI Agents SDK is OpenAI's runtime for those agents. It ships as` openai-agents` on PyPI and` @openai/agents` on npm. Both repositories carry the MIT license.


The docs describe agents as "LLMs equipped with instructions and tools." The SDK wraps them in a loop that runs until the task completes. By default, the SDK calls OpenAI models through the Responses API. The latest stable TypeScript release is 0.22.0, dated November 12 on the[JS releases page](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-js/releases) .


## Core primitives of the OpenAI Agents SDK


As of November 2026, the official Python and TypeScript docs describe these building blocks:


Primitive What it does When to use it


Agent Wraps a model with instructions, tools, handoffs, and guardrails Every build starts here


Tools (` @tool` ,` function_tool` ) Turns a Python function into a tool with a generated schema and Pydantic validation The agent needs data or actions outside the model


Handoffs (` handoff()` ) Transfers the conversation to a specialist, which becomes the active agent A triage step routes requests


Agents as tools (` Agent.as_tool()` ) Lets a manager call specialists and keep control Bounded subtasks under one orchestrator


Guardrails Validates input or output and halts the run when a tripwire fires Blocking off-topic or unsafe requests


Sessions (` SQLiteSession` and others) Stores conversation history between runs Multi-turn chat without manual history handling


Tracing Records model calls, tool calls, handoffs, and guardrails Debugging, monitoring, and trace-based evals


Sandbox agents (` SandboxAgent` ) Runs the agent in an isolated workspace with files, a shell, and resumable state The agent edits files or executes code


Start with an agent and one tool. Add a` SandboxAgent` only when the agent needs to touch files or run commands.


## Prerequisites


You need three things before the first command:


- Python 3.10 or newer. Version 0.9.0 dropped Python 3.9.
- An OpenAI API key exported as` OPENAI_API_KEY` .
- For the sandbox steps, a Baseten Sandbox account, the` bl` CLI, and values for` BL_WORKSPACE` and` BL_API_KEY` .


With those in place, start with the install.


## How to build your first agent with the OpenAI Agents SDK in Python


You install one package, decorate a function as a tool, then add routing, validation, memory, and tracing. Every snippet in this OpenAI Agents SDK tutorial comes from the official Python docs or examples.


### Install the SDK and set your API key


Shell
` pip install openai-agents`
` export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...`


On Windows PowerShell, use` $env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "sk-..."` . The SDK reads the key when it first creates an OpenAI client. Set it before your first model call, or call` set_default_openai_key()` in code. Run` pip show openai-agents` to confirm you have 0.24.0, the version these examples assume.


The import name is` agents` . A local file called` agents.py` can shadow the installed package and produce` ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'agents'` . A reply in one[OpenAI community forum thread](https://community.openai.com/t/modulenotfounderror-no-module-named-agents/1141761) suggests this cause. Rename the file if you hit it.


### Build a minimal agent with one tool


The[official quickstart](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/quickstart) uses` @tool` , an alias for` function_tool` :


Python
` import asyncio`
` from agents import Agent, Runner`
` from agents.decorators import tool`


` @tool`
` def history_fun_fact() -> str:`
` """Return a short history fact."""`
` return "Sharks are older than trees."`


` agent = Agent(`
` name="History Tutor",`
` instructions="Answer history questions clearly. Use history_fun_fact when it helps.",`
` tools=\[history_fun_fact\],`
` )`


` async def main():`
` result = await Runner.run(`
` agent,`
` "Tell me something surprising about ancient life on Earth.",`
` )`
` print(result.final_output)`


` if __name__ == "__main__":`
` asyncio.run(main())`


The decorator builds the tool schema from the signature and uses the docstring as the description.` Runner.run` calls the model, executes any tool call, and loops until a final output appears. If the run exceeds` max_turns` , the runner raises` MaxTurnsExceeded` . The printed result is the model's answer, so it varies between runs.


### Add a handoff and an input guardrail


A handoff lets a triage agent pass the conversation to a specialist. The[handoffs guide](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/handoffs) shows the pattern:


Python
` from agents import Agent, handoff`


` billing_agent = Agent(name="Billing agent")`
` refund_agent = Agent(name="Refund agent")`


` triage_agent = Agent(name="Triage agent", handoffs=\[billing_agent, handoff(refund_agent)\])`


The model sees each handoff as a tool. By default, the receiving agent sees the entire conversation history. Trim it with` input_filter` .


A guardrail returns a` GuardrailFunctionOutput` . If` tripwire_triggered` is true, the runner raises` InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered` and halts. The[guardrails docs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/guardrails) use a homework detector. Both snippets are excerpts, so copy the imports,` guardrail_agent` ,` agent` , and` main()` from that page:


Python
` @input_guardrail`
` async def math_guardrail(`
` ctx: RunContextWrapper\[None\], agent: Agent, input: str | list\[TResponseInputItem\]`
` ) -> GuardrailFunctionOutput:`
` result = await Runner.run(guardrail_agent, input, context=ctx.context)`


```text
`return GuardrailFunctionOutput(`
`output_info=result.final_output,`
`tripwire_triggered=result.final_output.is_math_homework,`
`)`


```


Python
` try:`
` await Runner.run(agent, "Hello, can you help me solve for x: 2x + 3 = 11?")`
` print("Guardrail didn't trip - this is unexpected")`


```text
`except InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered:`
`print("Math homework guardrail tripped")`


```


When the` except` block catches the tripwire exception, the example prints` Math homework guardrail tripped` . Input guardrails run only for the first agent in a chain. By default, guardrails run in parallel with the agent, so the agent can spend tokens before cancellation. Set` run_in_parallel=False` to block until the check finishes.


### Add a session for conversation memory


Sessions store conversation history so you don't need to pass` .to_input_list()` output between turns. The[sessions overview](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions) shows SQLite. The last line uses` await` , so run it inside an async function such as` main()` :


Python
` from agents import SQLiteSession`


` # In-memory database (lost when process ends)`
` session = SQLiteSession("user_123")`


` # Persistent file-based database`
` session = SQLiteSession("user_123", "conversations.db")`


` # Use the session`
` result = await Runner.run(agent, "Hello", session=session)`


The session persists conversation items keyed by session ID. If a run pauses for approval, resume it from a` RunState` , as the[running agents docs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/running_agents) describe. The session ID selects history but doesn't authenticate users, so your application must authorize access. For shared workers, the docs list` RedisSession` ,` SQLAlchemySession` ,` MongoDBSession` , and` DaprSession` .` EncryptedSession` wraps any backend.


### Inspect runs with tracing


Tracing is on by default. Each run records model generations, tool calls, handoffs, guardrails, and custom spans. Open the Traces dashboard on the OpenAI platform to inspect them.[Trace grading](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/trace-grading) runs graders against selected traces.


You can turn tracing off in three ways:


- Set` OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING=1` globally.
- Call` set_tracing_disabled(True)` in code.
- Set` RunConfig.tracing_disabled` for a single run.


` trace_include_sensitive_data` defaults to true, so spans store model and tool inputs and outputs. Set it to false to drop them. Per the[tracing docs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tracing) , tracing is unavailable for organizations using OpenAI's APIs under a Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policy. Those organizations can route spans to their own backend with` set_trace_processors()` . Check whether your organization falls under that policy before you rely on traces.


## Why agent-generated code needs isolation


Agent-generated Python runs without any human review. OWASP (Open Worldwide Application Security Project) names this risk in[LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm052025-improper-output-handling) . Its first example is model output passed straight into a shell,` exec` , or` eval` , which leads to remote code execution. Its guidance is to "Treat the model as any other user, adopting a zero-trust approach."


- Running that code on the host exposes your API keys, filesystem, and network. Containers narrow the exposure but share the host kernel. A runc flaw,[CVE-2024-21626](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-21626) , let a container process reach the host filesystem.
- [Firecracker microVMs](https://blaxel.ai/blog/serverless-vs-containers-vs-micro-vms-ai-agents) give each workload its own guest kernel behind hardware virtualization. The Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) calls them "appropriate for agents executing untrusted code" in its[Agentic Universe note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/agentic-universe-april-2026-v1.pdf) .


Separate-kernel isolation has limits. A[CSA research note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-pwnescape-linux-kernel-vm-escape-agent-san) says a microVM "still depends on host kernel hygiene." Isolation also can't stop an authorized process from sending data out. Pair it with an egress allowlist and proxy-based secret injection. The[sandbox agents quickstart](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox_agents/) warns that the SDK's local` UnixLocalSandboxClient` adds no OS-level confinement on Linux.


Run generated code in a microVM, away from the process that holds your credentials.


## How to run generated code in an OpenAI Agents SDK sandbox


Baseten Sandboxes are a first-class sandbox provider in the OpenAI Agents SDK. Configure credentials, connect the sandbox client, then run the agent and check its output.


### Configure Baseten Sandbox credentials


The steps come from the[Baseten Sandbox tutorial](https://docs.blaxel.ai/Tutorials/OpenAI-Agents-SDK) , last modified September 25, 2026:


Shell
` bl login`
` mkdir sandbox-agent && cd sandbox-agent`
` python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate # if new project`
` pip install openai-agents\[blaxel\]`


Shell
` export OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here`
` export BL_API_KEY=your_key_here`
` export BL_WORKSPACE=your_workspace_name_here`


The tutorial pins no SDK version. TypeScript users install` @openai/agents-extensions @blaxel/core` instead.


### Connect the sandbox to your agent


Each Baseten Sandbox is a Firecracker microVM with its own kernel. The SDK client for Baseten Sandboxes keeps the name` BlaxelSandboxClient` . The[sandbox clients page](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox/clients) lists other hosted providers too. It notes that "the same` SandboxAgent` definition usually carries over and only the sandbox client changes in` SandboxRunConfig` ."


The tutorial's` main.py` , verbatim:


Python
` import asyncio`
` from agents import ModelSettings, Runner`
` from agents.run import RunConfig`
` from agents.sandbox import Manifest, SandboxAgent, SandboxRunConfig`
` from agents.extensions.sandbox import BlaxelSandboxClient, BlaxelSandboxClientOptions`


` async def main():`


```text
`agent = SandboxAgent(`
`name="Sandboxed agent",`
`model="gpt-5.4",`
`instructions=(`
`"You have access to a sandbox environment. You can execute commands, manage files, and inspect processes inside the sandbox."`
`),`
`model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="auto"),`
`default_manifest=Manifest(root="/blaxel"),`
`)`


`client = BlaxelSandboxClient()`
`run_config = RunConfig(`
`sandbox=SandboxRunConfig(`
`client=client,`
`options=BlaxelSandboxClientOptions(`
`name="agent-sandbox-01",`
`image="blaxel/base-image",`
`region="us-pdx-1",`
`memory=4096,`
`),`
`)`
`)`


`result = await Runner.run(agent, "Install a complete Go development environment. Once done, return the installed Go version number and Go environment variables.", run_config=run_config)`
`print(result.final_output)`


`await client.close()`


```


` if __name__ == "__main__":`
` asyncio.run(main())`


Here's what each block does:


- **Agent definition:**` SandboxAgent` adds a workspace rooted at` /blaxel` through` default_manifest` .
- **Client and options:**` BlaxelSandboxClient` reads your credentials, and the options set the name, image, region, and memory in MB.
- **Run config:**` SandboxRunConfig` attaches the client at run time, so the agent definition stays portable.
- **Cleanup:**` client.close()` releases the client after the run.


The agent definition usually stays the same if you switch sandbox providers.


### Run the agent and check the output


Run` python main.py` . The tutorial shows this partial output:


` Go is installed and ready.`


` - Installed version: \`go1.25.9\``
` - Command check: \`go version\` → \`go version go1.25.9 linux/amd64\``


The SDK deletes the sandbox when the run ends. Initial creation takes under a second.


The tutorial's coding-agent example passes` pause_on_exit=True` , which stops automatic deletion after the run. It also passes` ttl="30m"` , which sets a 30-minute expiration that deletes the sandbox.


A Baseten Sandbox that persists after the run enters standby after about 15 seconds of network inactivity. It resumes from standby in under 25ms. Standby carries no compute charge.


Use[Volumes](https://blaxel.ai/blog/ai-agent-storage-tmpfs-volumes-shared-filesystems) for long-term storage.


Measure resume times on your own workload before you rely on the 25ms figure.


## What the OpenAI Agents SDK costs to run


Pricing starts with the default model. The SDK's default became` gpt-5.6-luna` in v0.20.0. The[OpenAI pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) lists it at $0.20 input and $1.20 output per 1M tokens, as of November 16, 2026.


The run estimates use` gpt-6.1-sol` instead of the default, at Standard rates from that page as of November 2026. Input costs $2.00 and output costs $10.00 per 1M tokens. Token counts are illustrative assumptions:


Run shape Model calls Input tokens Output tokens Cost per run


Single agent with one tool 3 12,000 1,500` $0.024 + $0.015 = $0.039`


Triage, guardrail and specialist 5 25,000 2,500` $0.05 + $0.025 = $0.075`


By default, each handoff receives the full conversation history, so include those repeated input tokens in multi-agent estimates. Hosted web search adds $10.00 per 1,000 calls. Hosted code interpreter containers start at $0.03 per 1 GB session. Eligible sessions bill per minute with a 5-minute minimum. Tracing itself is free, per the Python tracing docs. Baseten Sandboxes use[usage-based pricing](https://blaxel.ai/pricing) . They bill on allocated memory while active and charge no compute during standby.


Log per-request usage from` request_usage_entries` . Don't base a multi-agent budget on a single-agent test.


## Is the OpenAI Agents SDK production-ready?


Teams can run the SDK in production today if they pin versions and test every upgrade.


- The SDK is pre-1.0 and changes fast. The[release policy](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/release) says minor versions carry breaking changes. Version 0.21.0, for example, required custom` http_client` code to move from` httpx` to` httpx2` . PyPI's release history shows 11 releases in May 2026 and seven in July, by UTC upload date. Alpha previews ship through GitHub Releases only.
- The SDK supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) through four[MCP server options](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/mcp/) :` HostedMCPTool` ,` MCPServerStreamableHttp` ,` MCPServerSse` , and` MCPServerStdio` . The docs note that the MCP project has deprecated Server-Sent Events (SSE). Hosted MCP works only with OpenAI models that support the Responses API.
- Non-OpenAI models can run through LiteLLM. The SDK supports it "on a best-effort, beta basis," per the[models docs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/models/) . Many providers lack the Responses API, so call` set_default_openai_api("chat_completions")` . A[user-reported issue](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues/194) shows hosted tools failing under Chat Completions.


For tests, use` ScriptedModel` from` agents.testing` , the main utility in the testing docs. Trace grading works on whole traces. As of October 2025,[Latent Space reported](https://latent.space/wiki/sherwin-wu-4fc2967c) that per-span grading was still roadmap work. Watch the issue tracker for open bugs.[Issue #5642](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues/5642) , for example, reports that after a` conversation_id` run stops at` max_turns` , every later turn returns HTTP 400.


## Conclusion


You now have a path from` pip install openai-agents` to an agent with a tool, handoff, guardrail, session, and traces. The same agent becomes a` SandboxAgent` when it needs to run code, with Baseten Sandboxes as the sandbox provider. Next, adapt the tutorial's` main.py` to your own task, with` BL_WORKSPACE` and` BL_API_KEY` set.


## FAQs about the OpenAI Agents SDK


### Is the OpenAI Agents SDK free?


Yes. The Python and TypeScript packages are open source under the MIT license. You pay for model tokens at OpenAI API rates. You also pay for hosted tools such as web search and code interpreter, plus any sandbox compute your agents use.


### Can the OpenAI Agents SDK use non-OpenAI models?


Yes. Install` openai-agents\[litellm\]` and use` litellm/...` model names. The SDK supports that route on a beta basis. You can also point an OpenAI-compatible client at another provider. If the provider lacks the Responses API, switch to Chat Completions. Hosted tools and structured outputs then depend on the provider.


### Should I use Python or TypeScript?


Use the language your team already ships. Both SDKs share the same primitives, from agents and handoffs to tracing and sandbox agents. Names differ slightly, such as` function_tool` in Python and` tool()` in TypeScript. The TypeScript SDK needs Node.js 22 or later, Deno, or Bun.


### Which sandbox providers does the OpenAI Agents SDK support?


The Python sandbox clients page lists seven hosted platforms: Baseten Sandboxes, Cloudflare, Databricks, Daytona, E2B, Modal, and Vercel. Baseten Sandboxes are a first-class sandbox provider through the` BlaxelSandboxClient` class. For local work, the SDK ships` UnixLocalSandboxClient` and` DockerSandboxClient` . Runloop still ships in 0.24.0, but[PR #5369](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/pull/5369) removed it from the main branch.


### Is the OpenAI Agents SDK stable?


Not yet. Both SDKs are still pre-1.0. PyPI lists Python at 0.24.0 and the JS releases page lists TypeScript at 0.22.0, as of November 2026. Minor releases carry breaking changes under OpenAI's release policy. Pin an exact minor version, read the changelog, and run` ScriptedModel` tests on each upgrade.
